errors.meaning: The resignation is not awaiting approval.

planningRules.rule: Report the leaving date and the notice period to the employee's own account of it. A leaver who does not know their own last day cannot plan a handover (BR-4).
Report the handover checklist in full. Every timetable slot, section in charge, exam subject and activity has to be reassigned before the leaving date, and none of it releases itself (BR-5, BR-7).
Report the outstanding marks separately. The subject stays open and the exam cannot be locked until they are entered or transferred (BR-6, E6) — it is the item most likely to be missed.
Never revoke access at approval. Through the notice period the employee stays active and continues to appear in attendance, leave and payroll; the login goes on the last working day (BR-10).
Never reassign anything as part of the approval. Each item is handed to a named person who can actually take it, and a slot handed to a teacher already teaching then leaves it unstaffed (E5).

intent.summary: Release a leaver's settlement once the handover is clear. Accounts, one step, and the money goes.

steps.note: One step, and it is the last one. Once the money is paid the school has no hold left over anything the leaver still holds (E9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A release before the handover is clear is refused by the API.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the payment, the ledger posting and the closure of any recovered advance together or not at all. The staff record is deactivated and never deleted, because payroll history, ledger entries and audit trails all reference it — the employee drops out of payroll runs and out of the timetable (BR-13). An experience or service letter is issued to the employee, though the certificate module currently issues for students only and has to be extended (BR-12, E10).

Report any advance still outstanding after the recovery. It does not lapse — it is written off with approval or pursued (UC-12-05 BR-10).
